"Create a playable 2D anime-style turn-based gacha RPG called \"Eclipse\".

Game Style:

- High-quality Japanese anime fantasy art style.
- Beautiful anime characters with detailed costumes and weapons.
- Flashy combat animations, glowing weapons, magical effects, and powerful ultimate skills.
- Dark fantasy world with heroes, demons, knights, and powerful bosses.

Combat System:

- Create a 4 vs 4 turn-based battle system.
- Characters take turns based on their speed stats.
- Each character has three unique skills: basic attack, special skill, and ultimate skill.
- Include critical hits, buffs, debuffs, healing, shields, and elemental advantages.
- Ultimate skills should feature dramatic anime-style animations, camera movement, and powerful visual effects.
- Include both manual and automatic battle modes.

Gacha System:

- Create a character summoning system with three rarities: R, SR, and SSR.
- SSR characters should be rare, visually impressive, and significantly stronger.
- Allow single summons and 10-pull summons.
- Display exciting summoning animations with different colors for each rarity.
- Players earn summoning currency by completing battles and quests.
- Do not require real-money purchases.

Character Progression:

- Characters gain experience and level up.
- Add equipment, weapon upgrades, and character awakening.
- Each character has unique abilities and combat roles.
- Include a character collection screen and a team formation system.

Game Modes:

- Story mode with progressively difficult stages.
- Roguelike dungeon mode with random enemies, rewards, and upgrades.
- Challenging boss battles with rare equipment rewards.

User Interface:

- Anime-style main menu.
- Character collection, summoning, inventory, and battle screens.
- Display HP bars, skill cooldowns, turn order, and damage numbers.

Important:
Make this a playable game, not just a visual demonstration. Prioritize functional turn-based combat, character summoning, and progression. If the full game is too complex, create a working prototype with four playable characters, four enemies, one boss, and a functional gacha system. (2D Game, Phone/Tablet)

- Four-versus-four battles with speed-based turns, three skills per character, elemental advantages, critical hits, buffs/debuffs, healing, shields, ultimates, and manual/auto modes.

- Character collection, squad formation, leveling, equipment upgrades, awakening, story stages, roguelike dungeon, and boss mode.
- Anime fantasy presentation and mobile-friendly UI.

## Objective
- Build a playable, phone/tablet-friendly 2D anime-style turn-based gacha RPG called “Eclipse,” prioritizing combat, summoning, and progression.
- Deliver a working prototype rather than a visual-only demo.

## Requirements
- Four-versus-four battles with speed-based turns, three skills per character, elemental advantages, critical hits, buffs/debuffs, healing, shields, ultimates, and manual/auto modes.
- R/SR/SSR character summoning with single and ten-pulls; currency must be earnable without real-money purchases.
- Character collection, squad formation, leveling, equipment upgrades, awakening, story stages, roguelike dungeon, and boss mode.
- Anime fantasy presentation and mobile-friendly UI.

## Decisions
- Implement Eclipse as a standalone HTML/CSS/JavaScript game with localStorage saves and custom SVG character portraits.
- Prototype includes eight recruitable heroes, multiple enemy types, battle modes, and free-to-earn summoning currency.

## Work State
### Completed
- Responsive game shell and navigation in `index.html` and styling in `style.css`.
- Battle, gacha, roster/team management, progression, equipment, and persistence in `game.js`.
- Fixed mobile layout: `.main-view` now explicitly occupies grid column 1 at the mobile breakpoint; `node --check game.js` passed earlier.
- Tested battle start, stamina deduction, manual basic attack, auto mode, and victory rewards; victory granted 114 shards and 43 XP.
- Verified mobile layout at 390px viewport after fix: no document horizontal overflow; summon screen renders.
- Desktop reload previously reported no console errors.

### Active
- Test single and ten-pull summoning, team formation, and progression actions in the browser.
- Recheck desktop/mobile rendering and console after remaining tests.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Test single and ten-pull summoning, including currency and collection updates.
2. Test assigning heroes to the squad and at least one progression action such as training or equipment upgrades.
3. Recheck mobile and desktop widths and browser console; run `node --check game.js` again if code changes.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game entry point and app shell.
- `style.css`: Visual styling and responsive layouts.
- `game.js`: Game logic, content, saving, and UI rendering.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files were previously shown as untracked.
- Python HTTP server is available at `http://localhost:3002`.
- The mobile overflow came from `.main-view` implicitly occupying grid column 2 after the responsive grid collapsed to one column; explicitly setting `grid-column:1` resolved it.
- Battle was played through using auto mode to victory; summoning UI was opened, but pulls have not yet been tested. Team assignment and progression actions also remain untested.
